children: Colorado-based AI-native insurer MGT is expanding its coverage into California for small businesses and their agents.
The neo-insurer is expanding into the state's constrained insurance market, which has left many small businesses with fewer options for coverage, the company said.

“Small businesses are the backbone of the US economy and help keep the American Dream alive. Given that California represents 14% of the domestic market, it is essential to the success of our mission to insure America’s small businesses,” said Graham Topol, co-founder and co-CEO at MGT.
“At MGT, our combination of proprietary AI technology, admitted paper and A- AM Best rating allows us to step in as a reliable partner where legacy carriers won’t or can’t provide coverage.”
As of June 2026, California's FAIR Plan, or insurer of last resort, reached 697,000 total policies in force and $768 billion in total exposure across dwelling and commercial lines.

As some legacy carriers have pulled back from the state, MGT said it is using the opportunity to deploy underwriting models that allow it to evaluate risk at a fraction of the traditional cost while using property, geospatial and wildfire data to assess individual locations, giving the company greater ability to selectively write small commercial accounts rather than broadly restricting entire geographies.

“This launch opens a critical door for our distribution partners, ensuring that California’s entrepreneurs can finally access the comprehensive, rapid protection they’ve been waiting for,"  said Jack Ramsey, vice president of revenue at MGT.

MGT in October 2025 raised $21.6 million in an oversubscribed Series B funding round, led by Mubadala Capital. The round was also supported by Clocktower Ventures, Tacora Capital and existing investors.
At the time, MGT said the newly secured funds would be used to support research and development, deepen the company's vertical AI capabilities and expand its E&S growth initiatives across the US.
